passage: I'm Arnab. When Kalyani presented her project on rivers, she twirled the end of her plait round her finger, tugged her sleeve and straightened her collar twice. Behind me, someone whispered, “She doesn't know it, look at her hair.” I didn't agree. She answered every question the teacher asked, clearly and correctly. I think she was just nervous, since she looks like that every time she stands in front of the class. Afterwards I said, “Nice presentation.” She grinned and let go of her plait.

qa.q: What did Kalyani twirl round her finger?
qa.a: She twirled the end of her plait round her finger.

qa.q: What was Kalyani probably feeling, and what shows that the fidgeting was not proof of not knowing?
qa.a: Probably mild nervousness, since she does it every time she stands in front of the class. She answered every question clearly and correctly, so the twirling did not mean she did not know.

qa.q: What could someone do instead of whispering guesses about her hair?
qa.a: Notice what she actually says and, afterwards, offer a kind word, as Arnab did.

qa.q: How might Arnab feel about the whisper, "She doesn't know it"?
qa.a: Arnab may have felt it was unfair, since Kalyani answered every question clearly and correctly, and Arnab praised her afterwards.

grounding: Twirling hair and tugging clothing are self-comfort acts showing mild tension, not lying.

passage:
Monday: in the class quiz, Pema twirled her hair round her finger before each answer. Varun thought, She doesn't know the answers.
Wednesday: Varun stood to read his poem. His hands went to his collar and tugged it straight, and then his sleeve. He noticed, and thought, That's what nerves do to me.
Friday: Pema twirled her hair again at the quiz. This time Varun did not guess anything. He gave her a small thumbs-up. She smiled, and gave the right answer.

qa.q: What did Pema do with her hair before each answer on Monday?
qa.a: She twirled her hair round her finger before each answer.

qa.q: What did Varun think on Monday about Pema's twirling, and what changed his view?
qa.a: He thought she did not know the answers. After noticing his own nervous tugging on Wednesday, he saw the twirling was probably nerves too, and on Friday he felt sympathetic enough to give her a thumbs-up.

qa.q: What small step did Varun take on Friday?
qa.a: He gave Pema a small thumbs-up and did not guess anything, which was kind and gave her some support.

qa.q: How might Pema feel when Varun gives her a thumbs-up?
qa.a: Probably reassured, since she smiled and gave the right answer. She may not have known he noticed.

grounding: Hair twirling and clothing adjusting are self-comfort acts under mild tension, not signs of not knowing.
